gap: No result ChatGPT got puts Jackery's cycle ratings on the same 70%-capacity end point and divides them by today's price. Done that way, the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (1,024 Wh × 6,000 cycles) and the Explorer 1500 Ultra (1,536 Wh × 4,000 cycles) are rated for the same 6,144 kWh of lifetime throughput, yet jackery.com sells them for $669 and $1,079 today.
standout_why: I compared five pages. Notebookcheck's 1000 v2 page gives 4,000 cycles 'with a maximum capacity drop of 30%'. Notebookcheck's 1500 Ultra page gives '4,000-cycle rating (to 70% capacity)' and its surge. GearBrain's HomePower 1000 Plus v2 page gives 6,000 cycles to 70% and 3,600 W surge. Each page states only its own model's rating. None puts the 4,000-cycle Explorer line next to the 6,000-cycle HomePower v2 line on the same 70% basis, works out lifetime kWh, or sets either against a current price. 10adventures covers the old Explorer 500 and gives no cycle or surge figures. I couldn't read the ProToolReviews and Yahoo pages (both returned 403), and TechRadar's page text was cut off after the headline.
decides: For a roughly 1 kWh buyer, this points to the HomePower 1000 Plus v2 ($669, 6,000 cycles to 70%, about $0.11 per rated kWh of throughput) or the non-expandable HomePower 1000 v2 ($549, about $0.09 per kWh) over the Explorer 1000 Plus ($619, 4,000 cycles, about $0.12 per kWh). The Explorer 1500 Ultra only earns its $1,079 if the shopper needs its IP65 rating and 1.5 kWh in one box. Its rated lifetime throughput matches the cheaper HomePower 1000 Plus v2. Footnote for the page: the Explorer 1000 v2's 'one hour' charge needs an app-controlled emergency mode, and its default fast charge is 1 h 40 min.
